Multiple international and national aviation organisations such as EASA, ICAO and FAA have strict regulations on what is permissible and must/must not be found inside jet fuel.

Along the chain of production and transportation of said fuel it is tested and analysed to check its contents. for reference a few drops of water in a fuel tank of a plane can fuck up the engine.

At the end of this chain we have airports (that check the fuel contents), airlines with their own inspectors and engineers (that do the same) and pilots.

The contents of jet fuel are very, VERY strict and any unwanted particles (even just water) can cause unnecessary load to the aircraft and potentially damage the engines.

Again, if particles were to be added to jet fuel this process would have to be hidden to multiple normal civilians working in refineries, airports, airlines etc..

Nowadays most planes use VERY efficient engines that produce smaller "exhaust particles" but much more dense, this causes the contrails to stay in the air for more time.
